implementation_notes: Twirl, the engine shipped with Play, is the Scala default: a .scala.html file declares its parameters on the first line (@(title: String, rows: List[Row])) and uses @expressions, and the sbt plugin compiles it into an object with an apply/render method - views.html.orders(title, rows) is a normal typed call, so the marker/model contract is checked by the Scala compiler. Escaping follows the template's content type (Html) with @Html(...) as the deliberate raw escape, layouts come from calling a main template with a body argument, and the engine can also be used outside Play through twirl-api. Scala's own s"..." interpolation covers one-line fragments in code, but it escapes nothing and is not a page mechanism.
pitfalls: @Html(value) and Twirl's raw content types bypass escaping; they are the standard XSS entry point in Twirl views.
Template errors are compile errors, which couples the view to the model type in both directions: changing a field breaks the build until every template is updated.
Twirl compiles only where the Play/sbt Twirl plugin is wired in; reusing templates in a plain Scala build means adding the compiler integration yourself.
